newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end slightly higher, blue chips slide.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end slightly higher, blue chips slide.

text.p: Seoul shares ended Thursday slightly higher despite weakness in blue chips and large-cap stocks late in the day, brokers said.
The composite index provisionally closed 1.62 points higher at 700.22. Advancers and decliners were nearly neck and neck, at 384 to 379.

"The market is currently based on supply and demand, not fundamentals, which are still weak," said Choi Tae-hwan, head of sales at KLB Securities. He added buying has been rotational, with interest moving between blue chips, financial shares and those rumoured to be takeover targets.
Trading was quiet in the afternoon due to preparations for the Lunar New Year holidays on Friday and Saturday.

The bourse has been supported by rumours that the government would raise the foreign shareholding limit as early as in late March, liquidity injections by the central bank, and falling interest rates, brokers said.
But they cautioned poor economic fundamentals and the Hanbo Group loan scandal would remain a drag on the market's gains.
"I don't expect the market to rise or fall sharply next week," said Choe Seung-wook of Schroders Securities. "But it really depends on developments in the Hanbo crisis."

Hanbo Steel defaulted on debt repayments after accumulating some five trillion won in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions. State prosecutors arrested heads of two banks this week on charges of accepting bribes.
Midopa Department Store, Dainong Corp and Haitai Confectionary shares led trading on rumours they were targets of takeover bids. All three companies denied the talk.
Midopa gained 22,00 won to 30,700, Dainong climbed 560 won to 7,730, while profit-taking hit Haitai, which fell 1,100 won to 13,000.
Blue chips corrected after recent gains. LG Electronics fell 300 won to 10,900, Korea Mobile Telecom lost 5,000 won to 555,000.
The index futures March contracts gained 0.30 points to 72.80 while the underlying KOSPI-200 index ended 0.13 points higher at 73.59.
The market will be closed on Friday and Saturday for the Lunar New Year holidays.
